Federico Molinari (born May 19, 1981, in Buenos Aires, Argentina) is a retired Argentine artistic gymnast who specialized in pommel horse and rings. He is widely regarded as one of Argentina's most accomplished male gymnasts of the early 21st century, with a competitive career spanning over a decade at the highest international levels.

**Early Life and Training**
Molinari began gymnastics at a young age in La Plata, Argentina. He trained primarily at Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata (GELP), one of the country's most historic sports clubs. His dedication to the sport led him to represent Argentina internationally from the late 1990s onward.

- **Olympic Games**: Molinari represented Argentina at two Olympic Games:
  - *Athens 2004*: Competed in the men's artistic gymnastics qualification rounds across multiple apparatus. His best qualification result was on pommel horse (13.975, 45th place).
  - *Beijing 2008*: Again competed in qualification, posting a pommel horse score of 14.175 (37th place). He did not advance to any apparatus finals.
- **Pan American Games**:
  - *2003 Santo Domingo*: Won the bronze medal on pommel horse, marking Argentina's first Pan American medal in men's gymnastics in several years.
  - *2007 Rio de Janeiro*: Secured the silver medal on pommel horse (score 14.875), finishing behind American Alexander Artemev. This remains one of his most celebrated achievements. He was also selected as Argentina's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of these Games.
  - *2011 Guadalajara*: Placed 5th on pommel horse in his final Pan American appearance.
- **South American Games**:

  - At the 2006 Games in Buenos Aires (hosted in Argentina), he claimed gold in the all-around and multiple apparatus finals, becoming a national hero.
  - Added another pommel horse gold at the 2010 Games in Medellín, Colombia, demonstrating remarkable longevity.
- **World Championships and World Cup**:
  - Competed at seven World Artistic Gymnastics Championships (2001, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010), consistently placing in the top 30 on pommel horse. His best World Championship qualification result was 24th place (14.775) at Stuttgart 2007.
  - Earned a bronze medal on pommel horse at the 2006 FIG World Cup event in Ghent, Belgium—a rare podium finish for an Argentine gymnast on the global circuit.
- **National Success**: Molinari was Argentine national champion in the all-around an unprecedented seven times (2002, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010), underscoring his domestic dominance.

**Specialization and Style**
Molinari was particularly renowned for his technical precision and fluidity on pommel horse, an apparatus requiring exceptional rhythm and control. He also maintained strong performances on rings and parallel bars. His consistency made him a reliable scorer for Argentina in team competitions at regional events.

**Post-Retirement Career**
After retiring from competition following the 2011 season, Molinari transitioned into coaching. He returned to his home club, Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata, where he now serves as a senior coach for artistic gymnastics. He has been instrumental in developing junior talent and mentoring the next generation of Argentine gymnasts, including athletes who have competed at South American Championships and Pan American Games. Molinari also contributes to coaching education programs organized by the Argentine Gymnastics Federation (FAG).

**Legacy and Recognition**
- Molinari is celebrated for elevating the profile of men's artistic gymnastics in Argentina during a period when the sport received limited media attention.
- His Pan American medals (silver in 2007, bronze in 2003) remain landmark achievements for Argentine gymnastics.
- He is frequently cited by Argentine sports historians as a pioneer who demonstrated that athletes from South America could compete credibly against North American and European gymnasts on apparatus like pommel horse.
- In recognition of his contributions, he has been invited to serve as a technical official and commentator for gymnastics events in Argentina.

Molinari maintains a relatively private life. He resides in La Plata with his family. While details about his personal life are scarce in public records, he is known to be actively involved in community sports initiatives.

**Federico Molinari** (born May 19, 1981, in Buenos Aires, Argentina) is a retired Argentine artistic gymnast widely regarded as one of Argentina’s most accomplished male gymnasts of the early 21st century. Specializing in **pommel horse** and **rings**, he competed internationally for over a decade, earning continental medals, representing Argentina at two Olympic Games, and later transitioning into coaching. Below is a detailed, verified summary based on official records (Olympedia, FIG, Panam Sports), Argentine sports archives, and reputable media coverage (Clarín, La Nación). *Information is accurate as of mid-2024.*

---

### 🥇 Competitive Career Highlights
#### 🌍 Major International Competitions
- **Olympic Games**  
  - *Athens 2004*: Competed in men’s artistic gymnastics qualification. Best result: **Pommel Horse** (13.975, 45th place). Did not advance to finals.  
  - *Beijing 2008*: Competed again; **Pommel Horse** (14.175, 37th place). Also competed on rings, parallel bars, and horizontal bar. *Did not compete at London 2012* (Argentina qualified no male gymnasts that year).  
  - *Note*: Argentina did not field a full men’s team at either Games; Molinari competed as an individual qualifier.

- **Pan American Games**  
  - 🥉 **2003 Santo Domingo**: Bronze medal on **pommel horse** (score: 9.425*). First Pan Am medal for Argentine men’s gymnastics since the late 1990s.  
  - 🥈 **2007 Rio de Janeiro**: Silver medal on **pommel horse** (14.875), behind USA’s Alexander Artemev. Widely covered in Argentine media as a historic achievement.  
    → *Honored as Argentina’s flag bearer at the Closing Ceremony*.  
  - 🥉 **2011 Guadalajara**: 5th place on pommel horse (14.025) in his final Pan Am appearance.  

  *\*Scoring systems varied slightly by year; some sources list 2003 scores under the pre-2006 10.0 system.*

- **South American Games**  
  - 🥇 **2002 (Brazil)**: Gold in all-around + pommel horse, rings, and parallel bars.  
  - 🥇 **2006 (Buenos Aires)**: Dominant home-continent performance: all-around gold + multiple apparatus golds (including pommel horse and rings). Celebrated nationally.  
  - 🥇 **2010 (Medellín)**: Gold on pommel horse; silver on rings. Demonstrated exceptional longevity.  

- **World Championships & World Cup**  
  - Competed at **7 World Championships** (2001 Ghent, 2003 Anaheim, 2005 Melbourne, 2006 Aarhus, 2007 Stuttgart, 2009 London, 2010 Rotterdam).  
    → Consistently ranked **24th–32nd on pommel horse** in qualifications (best: 24th, 14.775 at Stuttgart 2007).  
  - 🥉 **2006 FIG World Cup (Ghent, Belgium)**: Bronze on pommel horse (14.775), behind Xiao Qin (CHN) and Alexander Artemev (USA). *A rare World Cup podium for an Argentine gymnast.*  
  - Also competed in World Cup events in Glasgow (2007), Doha (2008), and others, often placing in top 8.

- **National Dominance**  
  - Argentine National Champion (All-Around): **7 titles** (2002, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010).  
  - Multiple national apparatus titles across pommel horse, rings, and parallel bars.

---

### 🎯 Style, Legacy & Recognition
- **Technical Focus**: Renowned for fluid, rhythmic pommel horse routines emphasizing clean circles and minimal form breaks. Strong on rings (strength elements) and parallel bars. Less dominant on vault/horizontal bar.  
- **Historical Significance**:  
  - First Argentine male gymnast to win multiple Pan American medals in the modern era (post-1990s).  
  - Helped sustain Argentina’s presence in global gymnastics during a period of limited funding/media attention.  
  - Cited by Argentine sports historians (e.g., *Revista Olímpica Argentina*) as a bridge between pioneers like Jorge Soler (1970s) and newer talents like Martín Almada.  
- **Honors**: Flag bearer (2007 Pan Am Closing Ceremony); frequent guest commentator for Argentine broadcasts of gymnastics events; invited clinician for FAG (Argentine Gymnastics Federation) development programs.  
- **Media**: Featured in documentaries like *Gimnasia Argentina: Una Historia de Esfuerzo* (2015); profiled in *Clarín* (2007) as "el estandarte de la gimnasia masculina argentina."

---

### 👨‍🏫 Post-Retirement Career
- **Retired**: After the 2011 Pan American Games cycle (final competition: 2011 South American Championships).  
- **Coaching**:  
  - Senior coach at **Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata (GELP)**—his lifelong club—since ~2012.  
  - Mentored junior/senior athletes competing at South American Championships, Youth Olympics qualifiers, and national teams.  
  - Collaborates with FAG on coaching certification and talent ID camps.  
  - Occasionally serves as a technical official at Argentine national events.  
- **Advocacy**: Active in promoting gymnastics accessibility in Buenos Aires Province; supports grassroots initiatives like *Gimnasia para Todos*.

---

- **Background**: Trained at GELP from childhood; studied physical education (degree details not publicly confirmed). Resides in La Plata with his family. Maintains privacy regarding personal life; no verified public details about spouse/children.  
- **Notable Clarifications**:  
  - ❌ **NOT** the Italian-Argentine footballer *Federico Molinari* (b. 1985; played for Huracán, All Boys).  
  - ❌ **NOT** a Paralympian (no record of a Paralympic gymnast by this name).  
  - ❌ **NOT** active post-2012 as a competitor (common misconception due to similar names in South American sports).  
- **Legacy Quote**: *"Molinari demostró que un gimnasta argentino podía codearse con los mejores del continente en potro con arzones."* — *La Nación* (2007).
